title: On Sailing for the islands in March
subtitle: 江河湖海 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 江河湖海（自然生态·海洋与河流）
meta: 主题语境：江河湖海（自然生态·海洋与河流）　|　核心词汇：sail　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sail 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 the fisherman ① sailed for the islands in March without complaint, and every boatman in the harbour said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the fisherman ② sails for the islands in March with great care without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ sail for the islands in March at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ sailed for the islands in March before — a line in the logbook for July 1945 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Sailing for the islands in March without complaint, the fisherman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ sail the boat single handed with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Sail the boat single handed at once and never mention it again.

By 1958 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the logbook, and a new boatman from the next harbour ⑧ sails the boat single handed without complaint every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the pier, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ sailed for the islands in March again when nobody else would.

⑩ To sail for the islands in March, my mother said in 1963, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the harbour remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the harbour forgets, somebody sails for the islands in March with great care again and somebody must sail for the islands in March without complaint all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 航行（一般过去式 sailed for the islands in March：1951 年渔人头一回这样做，毫无怨言地）
B. v. 航行（一般现在 sails for the islands in March：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 航行（不定式 to sail for the islands in March：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 航行（过去完成时 had sailed for the islands in March：1945 年七月的航海日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 航行（动名词 sailing for the islands in March 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 驾驶（sail the boat single handed：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去驾驶一个人驾驶那条船）
G. v. 驾驶（sail the boat single handed：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 航行（后段两处：新来的船工照例 sails the boat single handed，而母亲又一次 sailed for the islands in March）

answers.why: sail 意为“航行”，1951 年渔人毫无怨言地航行三月里向那些岛开航，那是渔港里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 sailed。
sail 意为“航行”，自那以后渔人小心翼翼地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 sails。
sail 意为“航行”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯航行三月里向那些岛开航”，此处为不定式 to sail for the islands in March。
sail 意为“航行”，航海日志里 七月 那行字说明早在 1958 年之前就有人航行过，故用过去完成时 had sailed。
sail 意为“航行”，渔人说“航行三月里向那些岛开航这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 sailing for the islands in March 作主语。
sail 意为“驾驶”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去驾驶一个人驾驶那条船”，should ever 之后用原形 sail the boat single handed。
sail 意为“驾驶”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻驾驶一个人驾驶那条船（sail the boat single handed at once），以后再也不要提起。
sail 意为“航行”，新来的船工每个汛期都照例驾驶一个人驾驶那条船，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 sails。
sail 意为“航行”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次毫无怨言地航行三月里向那些岛开航，用一般过去式 sailed 叙述。
sail 意为“航行”，结尾那句是母亲 1963 年的话：要航行三月里向那些岛开航，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和渔港记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sail 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1951 the fisherman sailed for the islands in March without complaint, and nobody in the harbour forgot it.
Even now the fisherman sails for the islands in March with great care whenever the harbour asks.
Sailing for the islands in March without complaint, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever sail the boat single handed with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new boatman from the next harbour sails the boat single handed without complaint every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother sailed for the islands in March again, and the harbour remembered that half.
